evidence_quote: miR-103b was significantly increased in exosomes derived from TNBC-BM cells. miR-103b compromised the tight junctions of HUVECs and increased BBB permeability in mice.
rationale: The study directly investigates a molecular mechanism of breast cancer brain metastasis: exosomal miR-103b alters blood–brain barrier integrity and the pre-metastatic niche. It also identifies miR-103b as a potential therapeutic target, closely matching the profile’s interests in tumor progression and cancer treatments.
